Definition.Name: Incident response and escalation
Definition.Summary: Coordinate first response, diagnosis, escalation, and customer communication with explicit safe-refusal paths, artifact inputs, and emergency-governance notes.
Definition.ValueStatement: Shorten blocked time and preserve trust under ambiguity.
Definition.InterfaceContractSummary: Customer-facing response depends on reliable diagnosis and explicit decision rights.
Definition.GovernanceNotes: Critical escalations require approval notes and trust-aware evidence handling.
Definition.ChangeSummary: Refreshed to preserve the current concise baseline scenario while enriching diagnostic, approval, and mitigation discipline around the same three-step spine.
Definition.GovernancePolicySummary: Emergency paths stay bounded by approval, journaling, and evidence controls.
Definition.ConstitutionRuleSummary: Policy decisions stay explicit and reviewable.
Definition.OperatingModeSummary: Emergency operating mode is explicitly bounded by governance rules.
Definition.SimulationReadinessSummary: Seed pack models refusal, blocking, and artifact trust scenarios.

Roles.Purpose: Turn an incoming operational signal into a structured incident response posture with explicit severity, owners, and first actions.
Roles.StaffingIntent: A disciplined incident responder who can rapidly stabilize coordination without inventing unsupported conclusions.
Roles.SnapshotSummary: Initial incident coordinator for severity framing and first containment path selection.

Roles.Purpose: Investigate the technical fault path, propose mitigation, and execute or coordinate the change needed to restore service.
Roles.StaffingIntent: A hands-on technical responder who can diagnose the active failure mode and work with governance roles under time pressure.
Roles.SnapshotSummary: Primary technical owner for diagnosis, mitigation, and restoration work.

Roles.Purpose: Make the accountable go / no-go decision when an incident response path requires explicit approval beyond responder discretion.
Roles.StaffingIntent: A decision owner trusted to balance restoration urgency, risk, customer impact, and evidence quality during incidents.
Roles.SnapshotSummary: Explicit governance decision owner for risky mitigations and escalated incident actions.

Steps.Title: Acknowledge and classify incident
Steps.Subtitle: First response and safe-refusal posture
Steps.Notes: Capture the incoming alert, classify probable severity, and establish the initial response owner.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Inbound alert, customer impact, and available evidence.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Triage lead may safely refuse malformed or irrelevant incidents.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not let an ambiguous incoming signal bypass typed acknowledgement and classification.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Another triage lead may take over without invalidating the process.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Incident triage note
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for diagnosis, approval escalation, and post-incident timeline reconstruction.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must capture triggering signal, user impact, severity posture, responders, and first actions.

Steps.Title: Diagnose probable cause
Steps.Subtitle: Evidence-led technical assessment
Steps.Notes: Develop a diagnosis hypothesis and proposed action from logs, traces, and responder findings.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Resolver proposes action; approver decides emergency changes.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not present a mitigation as safe until evidence and rollback framing exist.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Resolver role may be rebound to another capable executor.
Triage lead validates communication impact before escalation.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Diagnosis evidence pack
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for approval, post-incident review, and recurring incident detection tuning.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Evidence must capture source and review status.

Steps.Title: Approve escalation path
Steps.Subtitle: Emergency decision gate
Steps.Notes: Approve, block, or refuse the proposed escalation or emergency change path.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not execute high-risk mitigation without explicit approval and rollback framing.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Escalation approval always belongs to the current approver role holder.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Escalation approval record
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for audit, post-incident review, and emergency change governance tuning.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Emergency change approvals must keep explicit rationale.

Warnings: Detailed sidecar metadata remains in the process-template pack files.
